lines: I
Your AI has never seen a folder.
II

Say you've given your AI tools: send a reminder, save a note. It asks the server holding them what it can do and gets one list back. Here's a real one. Thirty-five tools, in the order someone wrote them. No folders, no groups.
III

You say: save this. It wants a memory tool. The name is the first thing it reads, and three names start with memory. It takes one, a tool called memory recent. That tool only reads back what's already saved. Nothing is saved. Nothing errors. The note isn't there next time.
IV
Here's why. Nothing groups that list except the first word of each name. Where a tool sits means nothing, near or far.
V
Memory recent sits twelfth. The next memory tool sits twenty-eighth, fifteen unrelated tools between them. Only the first word says they belong together.
VI

Now the near one. The tool that saves, named write memory, sits eleventh, touching memory recent. But its first word is write. A look for memory tools finds three and misses the one that saves. That's the lost note.
VII

Thirty-five tools was never the problem. The problem is a list where only the first word groups anything, and the name that hurts got it wrong. Mostly this list got it right: thirty-two of thirty-five put the thing first, then the action. Tools sharing a first word are a family. That alone makes ten.
VIII

Nothing catches this. A thirty-sixth tool can start with any word; build passes, deploy passes. The AI pays, next time it reads the list. This one held because whoever added a tool matched the names already there.
IX

When you or your AI add a tool, start its name with the thing it acts on, and match the first words already there. Adding invoices? Invoice first, then the action: invoice get, invoice send. Not send invoice. Rename any that start with an action: write memory becomes memory write.
X
The first word is the folder.
facts: Source: devweb article mcp-tool-design. One real server's tool list: 35 tools, each only a name, a short description and an input schema; returned in written order with no sort, filter or grouping. memory_recent is 12th and memory_context 28th, fifteen between; write_memory (the tool that saves) is 11th. 32 of 35 names put the namespace first, giving ten families; three put the action first. Nothing in the code checks names. The save scene in beat III is staged: it shows what the list sets up for a model scanning by first word, not a recorded event; the article itself says it is a reading of the surface, not a measurement. Ticket family and a person-named tool are renamed generically. Fact trace: 31 traced, 15 advice, 1 flag fixed in version 05.
